NFL DFS Tight End Rankings: Week 9 (DraftKings)

DraftKings main slate · Sunday, November 8 · 11 games · By Chris Spags · · Numbers as of November 4, 8:53 PM ET

Brock Bowers is the top-projected tight end on the Week 9 DraftKings main slate at 17.7 DraftKings points for $7,900, at San Francisco. Trey McBride (15.8, $7,700) and George Kittle (13.7, $6,000) are next.

Greg Dulcich returns the most per dollar among tight ends projected for at least 7 points: 3.33 projected points per $1,000 at $3,100.

Every projection is a SPAGS model estimate from the November 4, 8:53 PM ET run of the Splash Play NFL model. This page updates each time the main-slate numbers are published.

Tight ends to know in Week 9

Brock Bowers, LV at SF ($7,900)

Brock Bowers carries the highest SPAGS model projection at the position, 17.7 DraftKings points at $7,900. That is 1.9 points clear of Trey McBride. The model gives him 8.5 targets on 32.8 routes. The salary works out to 2.25 projected points per $1,000, 11th of 18 at the position. Across 10,000 simulations Bowers averaged 17.9 points with a simulated floor of 4.3 and a ceiling of 44.0, and he holds 8% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. Las Vegas is a 10-point underdog on the road against San Francisco, with an implied team total of 21.25 in a game totaled at 52.5.

Trey McBride, ARI at SEA ($7,700)

Trey McBride projects 2nd at the position with 15.8 DraftKings points at $7,700. The model gives him 12.3 targets on 40.3 routes. The salary works out to 2.06 projected points per $1,000, 15th of 18 at the position. Across 10,000 simulations McBride averaged 15.8 points with a simulated floor of 3.3 and a ceiling of 42.6, and he holds 4% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. Arizona is an 8.5-point underdog on the road against Seattle, with an implied team total of 15.5 in a game totaled at 39.5.

Value: Greg Dulcich, MIA vs DET ($3,100)

Greg Dulcich projects for 10.3 DraftKings points at $3,100, which works out to 3.33 points per $1,000 of salary. That is the best rate of any player priced in the cheaper half of the 18 tight ends the model projects for 7 or more points. The model gives him 4.2 targets on 17.6 routes. Across 10,000 simulations Dulcich averaged 10.3 points with a simulated floor of 0.0 and a ceiling of 32.5, and he holds 18% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. Miami is a 7-point underdog at home against Detroit, with an implied team total of 21.75 in a game totaled at 50.5.
